title: CHAPTER SEVENTEEN. On Gods executive power; definition
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): 19:6. 11:17; Revelation 4:8; Luke 1:37; Psalm 91; Jeremiah 32:18-19; 35:11; 28:3; ye sacred writings sufficiently declare — Genesis 17:1; — that power stands as rightly attributed to God. that same which stands as Gods life by means belonging toward which, according to ye liberty belonging toward His will, He can work outwardly — whatever He can freely will, He works, whatever He freely wills — there follows ye power belonging toward acting. And these things also concerning ye will belonging toward God: On Gods executive power. CHAPTER SEVENTEEN.
pass_b_english: CHAPTER SEVENTEEN. On Gods executive power.

And these things also concerning the will of God: there follows the power of acting, which is Gods life by which, according to the liberty of His will, He can work outwardly — whatever He can freely will, He works, whatever He freely wills.
That power is rightly attributed to God, the sacred writings sufficiently declare — Genesis 17:1; 28:3; 35:11; Jeremiah 32:18-19; Psalm 91; Luke 1:37; Revelation 4:8; 11:17; 19:6.
source_text: CAPUT DECIMUMSEPTIMUM, De potentia Dei exsequente. Atque haec quoque de voluntate Dei: Sequitur agendi potentia, quae est vita Dei, qua pro libertate voluntatis suae extrinsecus operari potest, quaecunque libere velle potest, operatur, quaecunque libere vult. Potentiam Deo recte tribui, sacrae literae satis declarant, Gen. XVII.1; XXVIII.3; XXXV.11; Jerem. XXXII.18-19; Psal. XCI; Luc. I.37; Apoc. IV.8; XI.17; XIX.6.
